newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Dec consumer prices rise 2.2 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Dec consumer prices rise 2.2 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted December consumer price index remained unchanged on the month and rose 2.2 percent on the year to 136.8, Statistics Canada said Thursday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg Dec Nov
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.0 +0.4
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.8 +1.4
Statistics Canada said the all-items CPI rose 1.6 percent in 1996 from 1995. The agency calculates the annual average index by averaging the indexes for the twelve months of the calendar year.

The agency said annual increases in the CPI have remained at low and steady levels since 1992, ranging from 0.2 percent in 1994 to 2.1 percent in 1995. These increases were the smallest since the early 1960s.

The year-over-year increase in December was largely due to higher transportation charges, as well as higher prices for food, univeristy tuition, telephone charges, rented accommodation and fuel oil prices.

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally adjusted CPI to fall 0.3 percent on the month and the undadjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 1.95 percent increase in the all-items year-over-year index.
The December inflation rate was higher than the 2.0 percent and 1.8 percent year-over-year increases posted in November and October.
"The acceleration of inflation since September was due primarily to increases in the rates for auto insurance, gasoline, air fares and food," Statistics Canada said.

There was no change in consumer prices in December from November as higher prices for air travel, tobacco products, natural gas and fuel oil were offset by declines in the cost of clothing and footwear, food from stores and traveler accommodation.
